examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Amplitude-Phase Form for Sine
examples.problem: Write $3\sin x-2\cos x$ in the form $R\sin(x-\phi)$ with $\phi \in \left( 0, \dfrac{\pi}{2} \right)$. Round $\phi$ to $3$ decimal places.
examples.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
3 \sin x - 2 \cos x    = R\sin(x-\phi) ,
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
3 \sin x - 2 \cos x   = (R \cos \phi ) \sin x - (R \sin \phi )\cos x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\sin x$ and $\cos x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=3 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{2}{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{2}{3}) \\  & ≈0.588\,\text{rad}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Now, we find the amplitude $R.$ Squaring the first and the second equations of the system and adding the results together, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2} & =(3)^{2}+(2)^{2} \\ {R}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡ϕ+{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) & =9+4 \\ {R}^{2} & =13 \\ R & =\sqrt{13}.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we only considered the positive root, since $R>0.$

Finally, we can write the initial expression in amplitude-phase form as follows:

$$
3\sin(x)-2\cos(x) \approx \sqrt{13} \sin \left(x - 0.588 \right)
$$

feedback.problem: Given that the expression $\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=\sqrt{2} \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
